UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                   BEFORE THE
                     FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

    Mark Center Solar Project, LLC                     )            Docket No. ER27-___000

               APPLICATION OF MARK CENTER SOLAR PROJECT, LLC
                FOR ACCEPTANCE OF MARKET-BASED RATE TARIFF,
                CERTAIN WAIVERS AND BLANKET AUTHORIZATION

       Mark Center Solar Project, LLC (“Mark Center” or “Applicant”) hereby submits for filing

its proposed market-based rate (“MBR”) tariff, FERC Electric Tariff No. 1 (“Tariff”). 1 Applicant

respectfully requests that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission” or “FERC”)

(1) accept for filing the proposed Tariff in Appendix A, which authorizes Mark Center to make

wholesale sales of energy, capacity, and ancillary services at market-based rates; (2) grant certain

other waivers and blanket authorizations; (3) designate Mark Center as a Category 1 Seller in all

regions, except for the Central region where Mark Center would be designated a Category 2 Seller;

and (4) act favorably on this Application by issuing an Order no later than January 5, 2027.

       As explained below, per a misunderstanding, Applicant has already begun making

wholesale sales of energy and failed to obtain market-based rate authorization from the

Commission before doing so. As part of correcting for this inadvertent oversight, Applicant has

self-reported to FERC Enforcement and commits to follow the procedures outlined below to fulfill

lawful compliance requirements, as established under the Commission precedent cited herein.

Applicant is aware of the requirement to provide refunds for the time value of money consistent

with Commission precedent.

 III.      Request for Authorization to Sell Energy, Capacity, and Ancillary Services at
          Market-Based Rates

            A.       Description of Applicant’s Rate Schedule

          Applicant seeks to participate in wholesale markets regulated by the Commission by

transacting at market-based rates. The proposed Tariff would authorize Applicant to sell electric

energy, capacity, and ancillary services, including in the energy, ancillary services, and capacity

markets administered by PJM, to wholesale customers at market prices. Consistent with the

requirements of Order No. 697, the Tariff contains the Commission’s standard language that

commits Applicant to comply with the Commission’s regulations at 18 C.F.R. Part 35, Subpart H,

as applicable. 22 The Tariff also contains Commission-approved language that identifies all

limitations on Applicant’s market-based rate authority and any exemptions from or waivers

granted of Commission regulations. In addition, the proposed Tariff utilizes Commission-

approved tariff provisions with respect to the sale of ancillary services, as discussed further below.


            B.       Satisfaction of Criteria for Market-Based Rate Authorization

          In Order No. 697, the Commission established a market power analysis that focuses on

horizontal market power (generation) and vertical market power (transmission and barriers to

entry). A seller seeking market-based rate authority may show that it and its affiliates do not have,

or have adequately mitigated, both horizontal (e.g., using (1) pivotal supplier, and (2) seasonal

uncommitted capacity, screens), and vertical, market power in relevant markets. An Applicant

must also comply with the Commission’s regulations regarding affiliate abuse restrictions. Neither

Applicant nor any of its affiliates has horizontal or vertical market power in any relevant market.

 As discussed below, Applicant satisfies all requirements for the Commission to grant market-based

                   1.     Applicant Lacks Horizontal Market Power

        The Commission has promulgated indicative screen analyses and procedures for assessing

a market-based rate applicant’s ability to exercise generation market power. If the applicant passes

the indicative screen analyses, there is a rebuttable presumption that the applicant lacks horizontal

market power. In certain circumstances, the Commission has determined that an applicant need

not provide the indicative screens.

          As noted above, Applicant’s Project is located in Defiance County, Ohio. Consequently,

the relevant market for purposes of Applicant’s horizontal market power analysis is the PJM

BAA. 23

        In Order No. 861, the Commission simplified the horizontal market power analysis

required for market-based rate sellers by eliminating the obligation to submit indicative screens in

certain organized wholesale power markets that administer energy, ancillary services, and capacity

markets subject to Commission-approved monitoring and mitigation, including the PJM BAA. 24

Pursuant to Section 35.37(c)(4) of the Commission’s regulations, Applicant is relying on

Commission-approved market monitoring and mitigation to address any potential horizontal

market power that it might purportedly have in the PJM energy, ancillary services, and capacity

                  3.     There is No Potential for Affiliate Abuse or Reciprocal Dealing

         The Commission has traditionally indicated its concern that a public utility having a

franchised service territory and an affiliate may be able to transact in ways that transfer benefits

from the captive customers of the franchised utility to the affiliate and its shareholders. In Order

No. 697, the Commission discontinued considering affiliate abuse as a separate “prong” of the

market-based rate analysis and codified affiliate restrictions in the Commission’s regulations as a

condition of obtaining and retaining market-based rate authority. 31 Applicant agrees to abide by

the Commission’s codified affiliate restrictions as a condition of its market-based rate authority.

No. 697 and other FERC orders. 33 To the extent necessary, Applicant represents that it is relying

on Commission-approved market monitoring and mitigation to address potential horizontal market

power Applicant may have in those markets. 34

          E.       Category Seller Status

        In Order No. 697, the Commission created two categories of sellers: (1) Category 1 Sellers

that are exempt from the requirement to automatically update the applicable market power

analysis; and (2) Category 2 Sellers, defined as “any Sellers not in Category 1.” 37 A Category 1

Seller is defined in the Commission’s regulations as a seller that:

        (i) Is either a wholesale power marketer that controls or is affiliated with 500 MW
        or less of generation in aggregate per region or a wholesale power producer that
        owns, controls or is affiliated with 500 MW or less of generation in aggregate in
        the same region as its generation assets; (ii) Does not own, operate or control
        transmission facilities other than limited equipment necessary to connect individual
        generating facilities to the transmission grid (or has been granted waiver of the
        requirements of Order No. 888, FERC Stats. & Regs. ¶ 31,036); (iii) Is not affiliated
        with anyone that owns, operates or controls transmission facilities in the same
        region as the seller’s generation assets; (iv) Is not affiliated with a franchised public
        utility in the same region as the Seller’s generation assets; and (v) Does not raise
        other vertical market power issues. 38

Mark Center entered into an Energy Management Agreement (“EMA”) with a third-party,

unaffiliated entity (“Energy Manager”), who holds market-based rate authorization from the

Commission and has extensive experience in power markets. Under the EMA, the Energy

                        MARKET-BASED RATE TARIFF OF
                      MARK CENTER SOLAR PROJECT, LLC
                        FERC ELECTRIC TARIFF NO. 1



1. Availability. Seller makes electric energy, capacity, and ancillary services available
under this Tariff to any purchaser, except as prohibited below.

2. Applicability: This Tariff is applicable to all wholesale sales of energy, capacity, and
ancillary services by Seller, which are (a) subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission, and
(b) not made pursuant to another tariff on file with the Commission.

3. Rates. All sales shall be made at rates established by agreement between the purchaser
and Seller.

4. Other Terms and Conditions. All other terms and conditions shall be
established by agreement between the purchaser and Seller.

5. Seller Category. Seller is a Category 1 Seller, as defined in 18 C.F.R. § 35.36(a), in the
Northeast, Northwest, Southeast, Southwest, and Southwest Power Pool regions. Seller is a
Category 2 Seller, as defined in 18 C.F.R. § 35.36(a), in the Central region.

6. Compliance with Commission Regulations. Seller shall comply with the provisions of
18 C.F.R. Part 35, Subpart H, as applicable, and with any conditions the Commission imposes
in its orders concerning Seller’s market-based rate authority, including orders in which the
Commission authorizes Seller to engage in affiliate sales under this Tariff or otherwise
restricts or limits Seller’s market-based rate authority. Failure to comply with the applicable
provisions of 18 C.F.R. Part 35, Subpart H, and with any orders of the Commission concerning
Seller’s market-based rate authority, will constitute a violation of this Tariff.

7. Limitations and Exemptions Regarding Market-Based Rate Authority. Seller has
received waiver of: Subparts B and C of Part 35, except for sections 35.12(a), 35.13(b), 35.15
and 35.16; Part 41, Part 101, with the exception that waiver of the provisions of Part 101 that
apply to hydropower licensees has not been granted with respect to licensed hydropower
projects, and Part 141, except section 141.15; and received blanket approval under Part
34.Mark Center Solar Project, LLC, Docket No. ER27- -000 (2027) (unpublished letter
order).

8. Ancillary Services: Seller may make available to any purchaser the following ancillary
services:

PJM: Seller offers regulation and frequency response service, energy imbalance service, and
operating reserve service (which includes spinning, 10-minute, and 30-minute reserves) for
sale into the market administered by PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) and, where the
PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff permits, the self-supply of these services to purchasers
for a bilateral sale that is used to satisfy the ancillary services requirements of the PJM Office
of Interconnection.

Third-party ancillary services: Seller offers Regulation Service, Reactive Supply and
Voltage Control Service, Energy and Generator Imbalance Service, Operating Reserve-
Spinning, Operating Reserve-Supplemental, and Primary Frequency Response Service. Sales
                                        -20-
 will not include the following: (1) sales to an RTO or an ISO, i.e., where that entity has no
ability to self-supply ancillary services but instead depends on third parties; and (2) sales to a
traditional, franchised public utility affiliated with the third-party supplier, or sales where the
underlying transmission service is on the system of the public utility affiliated with the third-
party supplier. Sales of Operating Reserve-Spinning and Operating Reserve-Supplemental
will not include sales to a public utility that is purchasing ancillary services to satisfy its own
open access transmission tariff requirements to offer ancillary services to its own customers,
except where the Commission has granted authorization. Sales of Regulation Service and
Reactive Supply and Voltage Control Service will not include sales to a public utility that is
purchasing ancillary services to satisfy its own open access transmission tariff requirements
to offer ancillary services to its own customers, except at rates not to exceed the buying public
utility transmission provider’s OATT rate for the same service or where the Commission has
granted authorization

9. Effective Date. This Tariff is effective on such date as set by the Commission
